bug_semantics: GraphQL-Ruby’s `Schema.max_query_string_tokens` is a parse-time throttle (CWE-770) intended to reject maliciously large query strings. In the default Ruby lexer, `Lexer#advance` skipped `IGNORE_REGEXP`, which treated GraphQL comments (`#...`) as ignorable whitespace, then incremented `@tokens_count` only for the remaining punctuation/name/number/string tokens. An attacker can pad a small executable query with thousands of `# comment N\n` lines so the lexer still scans and allocates over the configured token budget while `@tokens_count` never trips `This query is too large to execute.` GraphQL-CParser is not affected: its ragel lexer `emit()`s COMMENT tokens and increments `tokens_count` before dropping comments from the parser token list. The limit was introduced in v2.3.1 and patched in 2.3.23 / 2.4.18 / 2.5.26 / 2.6.1.
flaw_origin: The incomplete throttle was written in the first `max_query_string_tokens` implementation, not a later regression. `c634445febcc93cf70bc4a38fe1f10aa2c40d495` added `@tokens_count += 1` in `Lexer#advance` immediately after `@scanner.skip(IGNORE_REGEXP)`. That IGNORE pattern already contained `#.*$` from the 2023 parser rewrite (`7f18613b523bed53f7623e9975e16a5ff898be2c`); comments were therefore never tokens for the new limit. The same PR’s C-parser follow-up (`8acc70892485da3a623afe955a3d875f2d8e14ec`) counted COMMENT via `emit()`, so the Ruby skip-then-count path was the flawed mechanism from first write.

reasoning: This is a real CWE-770 incomplete-throttling bug, not a withdrawn advisory: GHSA-3h96-34p3-xm76 is reviewed, not withdrawn, has no CVE alias, and the vendor patch plus regression test (comment-padded query vs max_query_string_tokens) match the described mechanism. Pre-limit, the Ruby lexer correctly treated comments as ignorable. The security limit was then grafted onto that skip, so comments were never budgeted. The smallest public first-write of that skip-then-count throttle is c634445febcc93cf70bc4a38fe1f10aa2c40d495, a non-squash PR member whose parent tree contains no max_tokens/tokens_count/max_query_string_tokens. The later merge 2f46e14ec, C-parser counting commit, and 2026 lexer comment-split fix are not BICs. Tag membership aligns: BIC lands in v2.3.1 (first affected) and the master fix 88d6c1ca / 2a8d956 lands in v2.6.1 with matching backports on the other patched tags. AI attribution is taken only from that BIC commit object: human maintainer author and committer, no AI/co-author/bot trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
